title: TagBO: LLM-Driven Task-Aware Graph Bayesian Optimization for Scientific Discovery
claim: A multi-stage pipeline fuses LLM-derived task-aware relational priors with structural descriptor graphs into one space for sample-efficient optimization.
layout: Multi-panel grid, top-down then left-to-right, gray curved arrows linking stages
description: A dense, color-coded block diagram. The top banner, "Problem Setup", shows the Suzuki coupling reaction, the yield-maximization objective, and three categorical variable lists (ligand in orange, base in green, solvent in blue). Below, two parallel branches run side by side. The green "LLM Guidance" branch scores semantic factors into a red-to-green ranking matrix, which becomes an LLM-induced graph. The blue "Structured Modeling" branch turns 33 physicochemical descriptors into a blue descriptor matrix and then a structural graph. Gray curved arrows feed both graphs into a purple "Graph Fusion" panel, which shows a fused graph and an MGDA box with ranking and graph-consistency losses. The fused graph leads to a "Joint Space" panel that concatenates the ligand, base and solvent embeddings. That panel feeds an orange "Bayesian Optimization" cycle at bottom left. Color coding by variable and by signal source guides the eye.
caption: Overview of TagBO on Suzuki coupling reaction optimization. For each categorical variable, TagBO constructs an LLM-derived task-aware relational graph from semantic rankings under the target task, alongside a structural graph derived from physicochemical descriptors. The two signals are fused to form a task-aware optimization space, which is combined with continuous variables and used for Bayesian optimization.
abstract: Mixed-variable optimization in scientific discovery often requires exploring large combinatorial spaces under costly experimental evaluations, making sample?efficient Bayesian optimization (BO) essential. However, existing BO methods typ?ically rely on structural descriptors to define similarity among categorical variables, implicitly assuming that structural similarity reflects similarity in task performance. In scientific optimization, this assumption is often violated, leading to surrogate representations that are poorly aligned with the optimization objective. To address this limitation, we propose TagBO (Task-aware Graph Bayesian Optimization), a method that integrates LLM-derived relational priors with descriptor-based struc?tural information for mixed-variable Bayesian optimization. Rather than directly using LLM outputs as predictive scores, TagBO treats LLM outputs as a potentially noisy source of task-aware relational priors and extracts coarse ordinal relational signals from LLM reasoning to construct task-aware similarity structures for scien?tific optimization. TagBO then performs constrained Gaussian process Bayesian optimization over the resulting joint discrete-continuous representation space. Ex?periments on diverse chemistry and materials formulation tasks demonstrate that TagBO consistently improves sample efficiency under fixed evaluation budgets across LLMs of varying capabilities.
